name: What is the best first step for ADU planning?

mainEntity.name: What is the best first step for ADU planning if I live in Los Angeles, Glendale, or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: What is the best first step for ADU planning if I live in Los Angeles, Glendale, or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: The smartest first step is not drawing floor plans from scratch. Start by collecting the property survey, any existing building plans, recent photos, title or easement information if available, and a rough budget and use goal. Then ask for a feasibility review that checks the site, zoning constraints, access, and likely design options. This early step helps determine whether the property is better suited for a detached unit, attached addition, garage conversion, or a more customized solution. It also saves time by identifying issues that can derail a project later, such as slope, access, or utility conflicts. Once the feasibility picture is clear, the design can move forward with much less risk. Homeowners who begin with facts instead of assumptions usually end up with better plans and fewer revisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best first step is to gather your property survey, existing plans, photos, and budget goals, then have a feasibility review before drawing full plans. That early review reveals what is realistic, what needs clarification, and what type of ADU fits the lot.
